name: Bulkamid pivotal trial
question: Is urethral Bulkamid injection noninferior to Contigen collagen injection for female stress urinary incontinence?

design.population: Women aged at least 18 years with stress urinary incontinence due to intrinsic sphincter deficiency or stress-predominant mixed incontinence; urethral hypermobility, prior bulking and stage 3–4 prolapse excluded.
design.locator: Full text, Elmelund 2019, Study Population, p 126; Sokol 2014, Results, p 845

verdictNote: Per-protocol and intention-to-treat composite responses met the 15-point noninferiority margin.
takeaway: In women with stress or stress-predominant mixed incontinence, Bulkamid hydrogel was noninferior to Contigen collagen for at least 50% reduction in pad-test leakage and daily incontinence episodes at 12 months: 75/141 (53.2%) versus 36/65 (55.4%) per protocol.

reports.label: One-year randomized comparison
reports.citation: Sokol ER, Karram MM, Dmochowski R. "Efficacy and Safety of Polyacrylamide Hydrogel for the Treatment of Female Stress Incontinence: A Randomized, Prospective, Multicenter North American Study." *J Urol.* 2014;192(3):843-849. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2014.03.109
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Methods, Followup and Results, pp 844–847

results.measure: At least 50% reduction in both 24-hour pad-test leakage and daily incontinence episodes at 12 months; per-protocol population
results.note: Prespecified noninferiority margin 15 percentage points; no confidence interval reported.
results.locator: Full text, Statistics, p 845; Table 2, p 847

results.endpoint: Composite leakage and episode response, intention-to-treat
results.measure: At least 50% reduction in both 24-hour pad-test leakage and daily incontinence episodes at 12 months; intention-to-treat population
results.note: Prespecified noninferiority margin 15 percentage points; no confidence interval reported.

results.measure: Patient-reported zero stress episodes at 12 months
results.note: Paper prints 50/99 as 50%; recalculated value is 50.5%.

results.measure: Patient-reported cured or improved at 12 months
results.locator: Full text, Results, p 846; Table 2, p 847

results.measure: 24-hour pad-test leakage at most 4 g at 12 months
results.note: Secondary endpoint; no prespecified success threshold.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, p 845; Table 2, p 847

harms.label: Procedure- or device-related serious adverse event
harms.note: Across both arms, 24 serious adverse events occurred in 22 women; only transient hematuria in the hydrogel arm was probably procedure-related.
harms.locator: Full text, Adverse Events, p 847; Table 4, p 848

values.exp: Any 58/229 (25.3%); acute retention 13/229 (5.7%); urinary tract infection 8/229 (3.5%); implant-site pain 28/229 (12.2%)
values.ctl: Any 32/116 (27.6%); acute retention 11/116 (9.5%); urinary tract infection 7/116 (6.0%); implant-site pain 9/116 (7.8%)

delivery.label: Injection schedule
delivery.value: Up to three urethral submucosal injections at approximately one-month intervals; 1–2 mL hydrogel per session at three sites, at most 0.6 mL per site, under endoscopic guidance and local anesthesia.

delivery.label: Repeat injection and total dose

values.exp: Second injection 177/229 (77.3%); third 82/229 (35.8%); mean total volume 3.3 mL (SD 1.6; n=229)
values.ctl: Second injection 77/116 (66.4%); third 30/116 (25.9%); mean total volume 8.6 mL (SD 7.0; n=115)

delivery.locator: Full text, Results, p 845; Table 2, p 847

reports.label: One-year patient characteristics analysis
reports.citation: Elmelund M, Sokol ER, Karram MM, et al. "Patient Characteristics that May Influence the Effect of Urethral Injection Therapy for Female Stress Urinary Incontinence." *J Urol.* 2019;202(1):125-131. doi:10.1097/JU.0000000000000176
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Exploratory Outcome Measures, pp 126–127

results.endpoint: Pooled post hoc cure and improvement
results.measure: 12-month SUI cure, improvement, or no effect in 291 post-hoc participants pooled across both agents
results.note: Cured: 74/291 (25.4%); improved: 164/291 (56.4%); no effect: 53/291 (18.2%). Cure required no diary SUI episodes and no ICIQ-UI-SF stress symptoms. One woman randomized to collagen received hydrogel. Among women at least 60 years old with fewer than 2.5 daily SUI episodes, 90% had a treatment effect and 38% were cured, versus 13% cured among younger women with at least 2.5 episodes.
results.locator: Full text, Exploratory Outcome Measures, p 126; Results and Table 1, p 127

results.endpoint: Age at least 60 years and SUI cure
results.measure: Adjusted odds of cure versus no effect at 12 months among 124 model participants
results.note: Reference: younger than 60 years; adjusted for daily SUI episodes, previous SUI surgery and leak point pressure.

results.endpoint: Fewer than 2.5 daily stress episodes and SUI cure
results.measure: Adjusted odds of cure versus no effect at 12 months among 124 model participants
results.note: Reference: at least 2.5 episodes daily; adjusted for age, previous SUI surgery and leak point pressure.
